# Browser Matrix Switchover Handoff Procedure

The switchover for browser matrix maintenance starts with the old entry point, not the candidate path. First, trace the known consumers of vdom-runtime and list the maintenance items that still go through the old entry point. Only then select a consumer that can roll back independently to try the candidate path. This leaves a migration record that others can continue from, rather than presenting the switchover as a closed matter.

```text
Before migration
Maintenance item ──> Old entry point ──> vdom-runtime Known consumers

After handoff
Maintenance item ──> Consumer inventory ──> Candidate path trial run
                              │                       │
                              └── Old entry point <── Independent rollback
```

## Sequence retained from the first draft

The first draft established only two things: first, account for the consumers and the old entry point; then have one consumer that can roll back try the candidate path. Keep that sequence. The consumer inventory establishes the migration scope; a single trial run establishes whether a consumer can take up the candidate path. A single trial run cannot replace accounting for the caller population, and the continued presence of the old entry point cannot replace a trial run.

This review breaks the handoff materials into a minimal reproduction, the corresponding build mode, and evidence of the first divergence. All three should be included in the same trial-run record. The minimal reproduction preserves the trigger conditions; the build mode identifies which build method was used at the time; evidence of the first divergence lets the next person start investigating at the first difference, rather than receiving only a sentence describing the final behavior.

## Selecting the first batch

During the inventory, register only the known consumers of vdom-runtime that can be confirmed through the old entry point. For each consumer, first confirm two things: whether it still uses the old entry point; and whether, if it needs to revert after moving to the candidate path, it can return to the old entry point without waiting for changes to other maintenance items. A consumer for which the latter is unclear cannot be in the first batch.

Include only one consumer that can roll back independently in the first batch. It does not represent the entire browser matrix; it only provides the first record of a reversible move to the candidate path. If behavior differs during the trial, save the evidence of the first divergence before deciding whether to keep investigating the candidate path or roll back. Do not write up the behavior as a conclusion first and fill in the divergence point afterward; that makes it impossible to distinguish whether the difference comes from the candidate path, the build mode, or the reproduction conditions.

When the candidate path shows no divergence, the minimal reproduction and corresponding build mode must still be included in the handoff materials. No divergence only means that this consumer showed no difference under the conditions at that time; it does not mean all other known consumers can leave the old entry point. The consumer inventory remains the starting point for the next batch.

## Handoff materials

- **Minimal reproduction**: The minimum conditions that show how the consumer reaches the old entry point or the candidate path. Do not leave only an outcome statement such as "switched over."
- **Corresponding build mode**: The build method used for the reproduction. For the same consumer under different build modes, do not use a single unlabeled record of observed behavior.
- **Evidence of the first divergence**: The point where the old entry point and the candidate path first behave differently; if there is no divergence, record the conditions under which none was observed.

Records that only relay the final behavior remain unconfirmed. They may suggest where to investigate, but cannot justify replacing the old entry point or expanding the trial scope. If only a conclusion remains in the handoff materials, first add the reproduction conditions and divergence point. Do not include that record in a completed batch.

## Batches and recovery

The migration does not clear the entire consumer inventory at once. After the first batch completes its trial run and a rollback decision has been made, select the next item from the inventory. Before each batch, check the old entry point again: if new known consumers have been added, keep them on the old entry point side first; do not mix them into records of completed trial runs. Older records need to show who was covered at the time, and later additions must not be incorrectly recorded as already migrated.

During migration, the old entry point is the recovery path. If the candidate path diverges and the evidence of the first divergence is insufficient to explain it, roll back independently and retain the materials from that run. Do not delete the trial-run record after rollback; it shows that the candidate path did not proceed further under that set of reproduction conditions, not that the consumer never took part in the migration.

Passing only the candidate path's final behavior to the next maintainer was an easy trap to fall into. Do not use that approach: without the minimal reproduction, build mode, and evidence of the first divergence, the final behavior can neither support continued migration nor ensure that rollback returns to a clearly identified old entry point.

## Review addendum

The review checks the handoff in the sequence "inventory, single trial run, materials, rollback." The old entry point and the candidate path are retained side by side to avoid presenting the candidate path as an entry point that has already replaced the old one. vdom-runtime is the existing lead on known consumers reused for this inventory; browser matrix maintenance items are still organized by the consumers and batches in the handoff.

If either the caller population or the rollback action is missing, the maintenance item remains in migration. When new observations are added later, first complete the minimal reproduction, corresponding build mode, and evidence of the first divergence for that run, then decide whether to move on to the next batch.
